_comment: What excludes a reader from a posting, as opposed to what merely scores
against them. Every entry here decides whether an opportunity is SOFT-HIDDEN
with a reason, so each one is a judgement about how much a stated demand
really excludes somebody — not a fact. They live in config so the judgement
is visible, editable and fingerprinted onto the assessments it produced.

basis: Only a doctorate demand excludes. A Master's requirement is a scored
shortfall on the education component instead, because employers routinely
accept equivalent experience against it.
Measured over the 4,402-posting corpus: 1,134 postings state a bachelor's,
396 a Master's, 326 a PhD and 61 a diploma. Treating a Master's demand as
an exclusion would soft-hide those 396 postings — 9% of the corpus — from
a bachelor holder who could in practice be hired into many of them.
A user living in the posting's country is not blocked by a refusal to
sponsor. The assumption can be wrong — a residence permit need not carry
work rights — and it is stated on the finding when it is used.
It errs toward showing the role: the opposite error hides a job the person
is entitled to hold, and they cannot ask about a posting they never saw.
A named language the user has not confirmed blocks. A fluency demand whose
language could not be read does NOT: it is reported unscored, because
guessing which language would hide a role over one the user may speak.
Measured: 436 corpus postings demand English, 148 German, 38 Japanese, 37
French, and none demands fluency without naming a readable language.
A national clearance is issued only to citizens of the issuing country, so
a non-citizen is excluded regardless of fit. Holding the clearance is a
separate question the finding says is still open for a citizen.
